reasons: Both answers give a full state machine, atomic Lua CAS slot capture, deadline workers and a webhook re-check, and both map all three bugs to concrete fixes. A's universal late-payment rule sends a refund for any succeeded webhook on a CANCELLED_* booking, so a duplicate webhook after a late (<3h) client cancellation would wrongly refund. B makes an explicit exception for no-refund client cancellations, and it also adds TTL'd cells with an ownership check at confirm, compare-and-delete release, and the admin-after-client-cancel conflict case. A's state table with per-transition guards is somewhat more explicit, but that does not outweigh the refund-logic hole.

A: Late/duplicate payment.succeeded rule auto-refunds any CANCELLED_* booking, including client cancellations inside 3 hours that must not be refunded
